episode_title: Every CFO Needs an Engineer | Ali Esfahani, Unconventional AI

real_qa.q: What is Unconventional AI's technical goal for reducing AI power consumption?
real_qa.r: Unconventional AI is trying to reduce the power consumption of AI systems by 1000x. The company has proven through research that you can build a computer using dynamical systems, taped out a chip that is much more power efficient than traditional computing paradigms, and proven that you can scale it. The plan is to complete the engineering phase over the next year and a half to enable cheaper and more accessible token production globally.

real_qa.q: How much did Unconventional AI raise in its seed round?
real_qa.r: Unconventional AI raised a $475 million seed round, later clarified as $470 million when Ali joined after the initial announcement.

real_qa.q: Why should every CFO hire a software engineer on their team according to Ali Esfahani?
real_qa.r: Every CFO should have a software engineer on their team as a partner to automate as much as they can. The goal is not to make humans irrelevant but to make humans more efficient and enable better work-life balance. With AI coding tools lowering the barrier to building applications, CFOs can now build custom tools that fit their specific workflows instead of fitting their work into rigid off-the-shelf software.

real_qa.q: What is Google's token processing volume as referenced by Unconventional AI?
real_qa.r: As of May, Google was processing 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month. At 10 joules per token, this equates to approximately 12 gigawatts of power consumption just for that one service.

real_qa.q: What internal tools did Ali Esfahani build at Unconventional AI using AI coding assistants?
real_qa.r: Ali built an AI-powered recruiting application to filter hundreds of daily job applications against job descriptions and company culture criteria; a research tool that digests Slack channels and classifies technical papers to synthesize engineer learnings; a knowledge base for EDA design tool documentation; a contracts management system accessible via Slack and Claude integration; and a personal AI assistant called Unassist that functions as his chief of staff.
real_qa.requete: Ali Esfahani internal tools Unconventional AI

real_qa.q: Why does Ali Esfahani believe software engineering demand will explode despite AI automation?
real_qa.r: Ali believes demand for software engineering jobs will explode because AI coding tools have lowered the barrier to building applications to a point where everything you can think of that will make your life easier, you can actually build. This will create distributed engineering needs across legal, finance, recruiting teams and so on, all building custom applications tailored to their specific workflows rather than fitting work into rigid existing applications.
real_qa.requete: software engineering jobs demand increase AI

guest.bio_context: Ali is a computer engineer by training who transitioned from Process to Unconventional AI after the company raised its seed round. Rather than taking a traditional CFO role, he negotiated an unconventional title and built a one-person product team that ships internal tools using AI coding stacks, while also handling finance, legal, investor relations, and recruiting functions across the organization.

real_quote: Every CFO should have a software engineer on their team literally they should be there and they should be their partner and they should try to automate as much as they can not because we're trying to make humans irrelevant it's because we're trying to make humans more efficient.
